en-US.shortDescription: Spoken market briefings: macro regime, rates, a morning brief, equity reports with a DCF fair value, portfolio risk and FOMC shocks.
en-US.fullDescription:
MacroPulse turns live market data into short spoken briefings for anyone who follows the economy.

Start the day with a morning brief: the last S&P 500 close, the macro regime, the 10-year yield and curve, SPY's quant signal and the latest daily scan's leaders, in about thirty seconds. Add it to an Alexa Routine so it plays every morning.

Ask for an equity report on a US company such as Apple or Nvidia: a discounted-cash-flow fair value built from SEC 10-K filings, bear, base and bull scenarios weighted by the current macro regime, a rule-based rating, and stop and target levels. On a Fire TV or Echo Show the headline numbers appear on screen. ETFs and foreign filers are declined rather than guessed.

You can also ask for the current macro regime (risk-on, neutral or risk-off) and the stress reading behind it; the latest 10-year yield, the 10-year minus 3-month curve slope and a credit-stress proxy; a Monte Carlo value-at-risk and expected-shortfall estimate for a ticker such as SPY or NVDA; an FOMC scenario stress test on a sample 60/40 portfolio; a volatility squeeze and breakout scan; or whether NVDA is in its danger zone.

Market data comes from public sources (Yahoo Finance and SEC EDGAR) and is never made up: if live data cannot be fetched, MacroPulse says so instead of guessing. The expected-return answer is a static reference estimate and is labelled that way.

MacroPulse is informational only. It is not investment, financial, tax or legal advice; fair values, ratings and simulations rest on models and historical data that can be wrong. No account or sign-in is needed, and it does not ask for personal information.
examplePhrases: Alexa, ask MacroPulse for my morning brief.
Alexa, ask MacroPulse to give me an equity report on Apple.
Alexa, ask MacroPulse what the macro regime is.
